# Start with your work

You can use Make the Case with an assistant or through its browser workspace. Start with a real frustration, one idea, several ideas, or a proposal that needs another step. You do not need a finished business case or the skills to build the entire solution.

## With an AI assistant

Download this project and supply the complete `skills/make-the-case` folder, including its reference. If your assistant can read repository links, give it the actual URL to that folder instead. Named-skill installation is optional.

During draft review, the complete instructions are at:

https://github.com/rtomboj/innovate-project-development-mode/tree/make-the-case-prototype-20261027/make-the-case/skills/make-the-case

The review-branch starting prompt can begin with:

```text
Follow Make the Case at:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtomboj/innovate-project-development-mode/make-the-case-prototype-20261027/make-the-case/skills/make-the-case/SKILL.md
Read it completely and resolve its references from the same branch.
```

Use `main` in those links only after the corresponding changes are merged.

Copy this prompt, filling in only what you know:

```text
Follow the Make the Case instructions in the skill folder I supplied.
Read SKILL.md and follow its references when relevant.

My company or team: [brief description]
My role and contribution: [what I do or know about the work]
What I want to improve: [outcome or problem]
My idea or ideas: [describe them; help me find one if needed]
Known constraints or evidence: [what is available; unknown is acceptable]

Begin with my context. Ask up to three focused questions at a time.
Keep every idea, develop one with me, and help me identify collaborators
and the next decision. I may not be the person who builds it.
Separate evidence, assumptions, forecasts, and achieved results.
Keep a contribution record and a continuation summary I can save.
```

You should receive questions grounded in your actual work, a scoped case, open evidence needs, an appropriate next request, and saved context. Correct the assistant where it misunderstands the work. Do not accept unsupported numbers merely because they sound persuasive.

## In the workspace

1. Inspect the clearly labeled fictional example. Select **What if checking takes longer?** and change the review time. See how the forecast and next decision change.
2. Choose **Start my own**. Describe the company/team, intended outcome, and conditions. Keep one idea or add several at once.
3. Develop one focus through Scope, People & permissions, and Evidence & cost.
4. Use **Prepare AI briefing** to copy your context into an assistant your organization permits. The briefing includes the selected idea and preserves the other ideas. Bring the useful reasoning and facts back into the fields.
5. Create a pitch, record decisions and contributions, and download the workspace JSON. Open that file later to continue with all ideas retained.

The workspace does not call an AI model, connect to your employer, or send messages. It uses your entries to calculate scenarios and highlight missing conditions. The assistant-guided method supplies the deeper discovery and case development.

## What to bring

A concrete example of today's work is enough to start. Timing, volumes, quality issues, current tools, and decision context help when available. Use permitted or sanitized information. If you lack baseline data or permission to test, the next request can be for time, access, or specialist review.

## Continue existing work

Supply your saved records and say:

```text
Continue Make the Case from these records. Preserve all ideas and
earlier decisions. Identify the next unresolved question or decision;
do not rebuild completed work. Update assumptions when I correct them.
```

Download a fresh workspace after material changes. Browser storage can be cleared or unavailable; an exported file is the portable copy.

## Share useful feedback

Which part helped you move forward? Where did an idea get stuck? What did the assistant misunderstand? What decision did you reach? Share a sanitized description through the newsletter's normal comment or message route. You do not need to disclose internal data or join a formal test group.
